title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Unreal C++ fundamentals, macros, gameplay programming, and best practices!

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using C++ over Blueprints?
questions.explanation: C++ compiles to native machine code, running significantly faster than the Blueprint virtual machine.

questions.question: Which macro marks a class for Unreal's type system?
questions.explanation: UCLASS() is required above class declarations for any class managed by Unreal.

questions.question: The _____() macro injects boilerplate code into a UCLASS.
questions.explanation: GENERATED_BODY() is required inside the class body to integrate with Unreal's reflection.

questions.question: What does the 'A' prefix in AMyActor indicate?
questions.explanation: Unreal naming conventions use A for Actors, U for UObjects, F for structs.

questions.question: Which UPROPERTY specifier makes a variable editable in the Details panel?
questions.explanation: EditAnywhere allows editing the property in the editor. VisibleAnywhere only shows.

questions.question: A UPROPERTY without EditAnywhere can still be modified in the Details panel.
questions.explanation: Without EditAnywhere or VisibleAnywhere, the property won't appear at all.

questions.question: Which UFUNCTION specifier allows a function to be called from Blueprints?
questions.explanation: BlueprintCallable makes the function available as a node in Blueprint graphs.

questions.question: What is the difference between BlueprintImplementableEvent and BlueprintNativeEvent?
options: ImplementableEvent has no C++ body; NativeEvent has a default C++ implementation
questions.explanation: BlueprintImplementableEvent is declared in C++ but implemented entirely in Blueprint. BlueprintNativeEvent can have a C++ default that Blueprints may override.

questions.question: How do you enable Tick for an Actor in C++?
questions.explanation: By default Tick is disabled. You must enable it in the constructor.

questions.question: To create a component in the constructor, use the _____ function.
questions.explanation: CreateDefaultSubobject is used in constructors to create sub‑objects like components.

questions.question: You must call Super::BeginPlay() inside your BeginPlay override.
questions.explanation: Calling the parent class's implementation ensures proper initialization.

questions.question: How do you spawn an actor in C++?
questions.explanation: GetWorld()->SpawnActor is the standard method to spawn actors at runtime.

questions.question: Which class is used to manage timers in C++?
questions.explanation: GetWorldTimerManager() returns a reference to the world's timer manager.

questions.question: What does a FTimerHandle represent?
options: A unique identifier for a scheduled timer
questions.explanation: FTimerHandle is used to reference and clear a specific timer.

questions.question: Which function performs a line trace (raycast) in C++?
questions.explanation: LineTraceSingleByChannel performs a collision trace along a line, returning the first blocking hit.

questions.question: You can use std::vector in Unreal C++ without any issues.
questions.explanation: While possible, Unreal provides TArray for integration with the engine's reflection and garbage collection.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to log messages in C++?
questions.explanation: UE_LOG outputs to the Output Log; it's the standard debugging tool.

questions.question: How do you debug C++ code during Play in Editor?
options: Attach Visual Studio to UnrealEditor.exe, then set breakpoints
questions.explanation: You attach VS to the editor process, then breakpoints in your code will be hit.

questions.question: What is Live Coding (Ctrl+Alt+F11) used for?
options: Patching C++ changes without restarting the editor
questions.explanation: Live Coding hot‑reloads modified C++ code, speeding up iteration.

questions.question: You should always use raw pointers (AActor*) for actor references.
questions.explanation: Use TObjectPtr (UE5.1+) or TWeakObjectPtr to safely handle actor references that may be destroyed.

questions.question: Which Unreal container corresponds to a dictionary (key‑value pairs)?
questions.explanation: TMap stores associative key‑value pairs.

questions.question: Where should Input Action bindings be set up in a Pawn/Character?
questions.explanation: SetupPlayerInputComponent is called when the input component is created, the correct place for bindings.

questions.question: What must be defined in Project Settings before binding an Action in C++?
questions.explanation: The action name must match an entry in Project Settings → Input (or Enhanced Input Context).

questions.question: You should include the entire engine header in every file to avoid missing includes.
questions.explanation: Use forward declarations and include only what's necessary to reduce compile times.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the GENERATED_BODY() macro inside a UCLASS?
options: It injects required boilerplate for Unreal's type system
It marks the class for garbage collection
questions.explanation: GENERATED_BODY() is required for Unreal's reflection and code generation.
